analysis.title: Risks vs fundamentals: where are the asymmetries?
key_insights: UBS Global Equity Strategy says market internals showed accelerated de-risking last week: defensives beat cyclicals, high quality beat low, low momentum beat high momentum, and Europe beat the US. The AI 100 fell 5% as Coreweave's CDS surged, while the ex-AI 400 rose 2.5% with every equal-weighted S&P sector up except Tech.
Bond yields fell last week even though CPI was hot and WTI oil rose 10% on Iran escalation fears. UBS reads the lack of a rise in rates vol as a good sign going into FOMC and the thick of earnings.

UBS sees rising odds of both a correlated rally and a selloff. Earnings, the FOMC and US midterms over the next 2+ weeks set the path into 2027, and Iran is an increasing overhang. Implied correlations are too low if Tech and ex-Tech/rate-sensitive segments can rally or fall at the same time.

The beta of risk premia to moves in rates looks higher after the rate spike, as shown by the CRWV CDS. UBS uses three frameworks to find relative asymmetries: an ML model of what overshot macro moves, REVS scores vs rates betas, and PEG ratios vs EPS momentum.

Circuit breakers named: AI demand, Fed path, oil/Iran, midterms and buybacks. AI demand remains the first driver of equities, but Fed rate expectations have gained importance in the ML model. A local peak in yields and rates vol is key for stocks.

Hyperscaler results need to show accelerating AI demand and operating cash flow (OCF) to push CDS spreads lower. META reports Oct 21 and MSFT, GOOG and AMZN report Oct 28-29. UBS analyst forecasts for US cloud sales over the next 4 quarters are ~15% above consensus, so upgrades could fuel another leg up in AI trades.

UBS expects US hyperscaler cloud revenue to grow 60% y/y in 3Q, up from 50% in 2Q, and to reach $574bn over the next 4 quarters, ~73% growth versus the prior period. Backlog diversification and AI monetization commentary will be key to the ROI debate.
Neoclouds account for ~7% of 2027 AI capex and have enterprise value of ~$130bn. UBS sees low risk to the broad AI build-out if AI demand is there, given core hyperscaler OCF and borrowing capacity.

Q2 earnings bar is low: nearly 70% of companies are expected to deliver slower EPS growth than in 2Q, and the median stock has derated 7%+ since the start of 2Q reporting. Estimates are up 1.8% (3.6% for Tech+ and 0.8% for ex-Tech+).

UBS's baseline is a benign Fed hiking cycle of less than 100bp. In the 2013, 2016, 2021 and 2023 episodes, ACWI and SPX rallied 8-10% on average over the next 6 months and 15-18% over the next year. In 1994, 1999 and 2022, when the Fed hiked 100bp+, returns were negative or flat over the following year.

The US 10-year has risen +1.5 standard deviations above its 1-year moving average only seven times in 40 years. UBS sees a case for the 10y to return toward 5% if data and catalysts fall the right way.

Equities have asymmetry to lower rates. The 10y is up ~100bp YTD to 5.1% and SPX NTM P/E is down ~20% since November, matching 1994. UBS's model-implied P/E is above 24x against <20x now, implying ~25% upside.

Rate-sensitive sectors overshot the ML model. In the US, Cap Goods, Utilities, Consumer Durables, Real Estate and Banks underperformed model expectations, and oil-sensitive Transports and Retail lagged more than implied.

UBS favors US Capital Goods and Transports (positive on all three frameworks). Banks, Utilities, Insurance and parts of Consumer Services are positive on two of three. It is negative on US Staples, Telecom and Materials ex Metals, and Energy and Software have outperformed their model-implied moves.

Start reducing Energy exposure: the sector is up over 50% YTD and has rallied more than forward oil prices, which UBS reads as a sign of demand destruction at higher oil prices. UBS prefers reallocating to Cap Goods, whose relative performance is back at 2-year lows.
US Utilities P/E has fallen toward 15x, near 10+ year lows, while Staples trade at ~25x. Utilities' earnings yield plus EPS CAGR is nearly 16% vs ~11% for Staples.
Europe: industrials are where revisions are accelerating as AI capex moves down the chain. EU Consumer Cyclicals are seeing negative revisions. European bank lending is growing over 4% y/y.

SPX has derated ~15% relative to the FTSE 100 over two years despite 22% stronger relative earnings growth. Korea has EPS revised up 15% over 3 months vs 4% for India, and memory-stock FCF is worth 80%+ of market cap over two years.
Midterm-year seasonality: SPX has rallied an average of 6% from end-September to end-December in midterm years and 14% through March.
Buybacks: Micron can buy back stock from Dec 9. MU and NVDA quarterly buybacks of $70bn are over 25% of SPX LTM buybacks. OCF is up ~$825bn y/y (+25%), pointing to larger buybacks.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield spike driven mainly by real yields and Fed hike pricing. Fell last week despite hot CPI.
No hike plus less hawkish rhetoric should lower rates vol, which is positive for stocks.

macro_indicators.reading: Up 10% last week on Iran escalation fears
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher oil raises demand destruction risk and pressures rates.
A benign cycle historically led to equity rallies.
Yields still fell, a sign of resilience.

macro_indicators.reading: <$90 in Aug to >$105 in early Sep
macro_indicators.interpretation: Spot rose while forwards stayed flat, which may reflect demand-destruction concerns.

trade_ideas.rationale: Positions for a broader correlated rally if rates/oil ease, midterms pass without a shock, AI demand holds and earnings and buybacks support.

trade_ideas.description: Buy HYG downside (puts, e.g. 1x1.5 put ratios) for yield-plus-spread 'double whammy'
trade_ideas.rationale: Treasury yields and HY spreads could rise together, with stress emerging first in lower-quality HY and leveraged loans.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SPX puts funded by selling XLU puts (put switch, for flat premium)
trade_ideas.rationale: Hedges a growth or AI disappointment. XLU downside vol is rich vs SPX, and Utilities have underperformed the macro model.
trade_ideas.risk: A correlated rate-driven selloff could still hit Utilities.

trade_ideas.description: Sell KOSPI2/SMH/SOXX puts to buy 2x notional SXXP calls
trade_ideas.rationale: Korean semis downside is limited by DRAM undersupply through 2028 and buybacks, and rich implied vol funds more upside in Europe.
SPX derated ~15% relative to the FTSE in two years despite 22% stronger relative earnings growth.
Korea has a stronger two-year EPS outlook and a lower valuation than India, with a current-account surplus buffer.

trade_ideas.description: Buy XLI Dec calls funded by selling XLP Dec calls (25-delta ratio call switch, ~0.8 XLI:XLP, flat premium)
trade_ideas.rationale: Works if yields and oil fall together. Staples have rallied >8% since 30-Sep and Industrials have stronger revisions.

trade_ideas.description: Long US Utilities over US Staples
trade_ideas.rationale: Utilities P/E near 15x and earnings yield plus EPS CAGR ~16% vs ~11% for Staples.
Positive revisions, light crowding, and 7% below macro-implied level, with a valuation held back by real yields.

trade_ideas.description: Long US Industrials and Capex Broadening basket (UBEQCPXB) over equal-weight SPX
trade_ideas.rationale: Basket of 48 stocks leveraged to capex broadening with EPS revisions near 2020-21 highs and lower crowding.

trade_ideas.description: Long EU Industrials (SXNP) vs EU Consumer Cyclicals (UBXECCYC)
trade_ideas.rationale: EU Industrials have positive revisions and lighter crowding, while Consumer Cyclicals have negative revisions.

trade_ideas.description: Long Higher Growth+CFROI at a Discount basket (UBEQHGCD) vs Expensive Fundamentals basket (UBEQEXFN)
trade_ideas.rationale: The discount basket trades at ~30% lower P/E with ~10pp higher forward sales CAGR and ~28pp higher CFROI.

trade_ideas.description: Cut Energy exposure and reallocate to Cap Goods/Industrials; opportunistically sell XOP upside to fund other upside
trade_ideas.rationale: Energy is up over 50% YTD and faces demand-destruction risk at higher oil prices.

risk_factors: Tightening cycle: an aggressive Fed hiking cycle (100bp+) has historically led to flat or negative equity returns.
Credit: an unexpected tightening cycle could hit lower-quality HY and leveraged loans first.
AI financing: the Coreweave bond yield and CDS spike raised worries about financing costs for AI capex.
Oil/Iran escalation raising oil prices and demand destruction.
US midterms are the largest risk in options-implied pricing.
Rates vol rising further, with the beta of risk premia to rates higher after the spike.
Utilities and rate-sensitive sectors exposed to higher bond yields, and expensive growth sensitive to the price paid.
charts_described: Figure 25 caption states positive revisions outperformed rising bond yields.
Figure 50 caption states the S&P 500 has derated by ~20% already, and Figure 51 states the S&P has ~25% implied upside on UBS's model.
Figure 30 caption states the correlation of oil vs yields is just off 15y+ highs (ex-Covid).
vol_and_positioning: Index protection is expensive to carry because high dispersion mutes index-level moves. This is typically exacerbated through earnings season.
Rate volatility has already well exceeded equity volatility in anticipation of further rate hikes.
XLU downside volatility is relatively rich vs SPX, which has historically reversed in large index drawdowns.
Credit spreads have stayed unusually calm despite higher rates vol. Yield vs HY spread correlation is just off all-time highs, a 'double whammy' UBS says is not fully priced into HYG volatility.
HYG skew has risen amid the initial drawdown. UBS suggests HYG 1x1.5 put ratios.
Korean semis implied vol is rich, which UBS would use to buy more than 2x the notional of upside in Europe.
Midterms pose the largest risk in options-implied pricing (data as of 16-Oct-2026).
Crowding in AI Capex is high and falling, in contrast to Industrial Capacity. Crowding is lower for the capex-broadening basket than the average stock.
geopolitical: Iran escalation fears pushed WTI oil up 10% last week and are an increasing overhang as US midterms approach.
Middle East and Ukraine conflict affect refined product prices.
The Middle East conflict has held back EU Industrials.
US midterm elections: polls close Nov 3, with results possibly confirmed in following days or weeks.

tension_points.bull_case: Rates and oil ease, midterm risks pass, AI demand holds, earnings beat a low bar and buybacks pick up after the OCF surge, so Tech and ex-Tech rally together.
tension_points.bear_case: An aggressive tightening cycle, a further rates spike and credit stress (CRWV CDS, HY spreads) could sell off Tech and rate-sensitive segments together.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed hiking cycle of 100bp+ within a year of the 10y spike, as in 1994, 1999 and 2022, when equity returns were flat or negative.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler OCF and borrowing capacity cover capex, compute demand exceeds supply, and UBS cloud forecasts are ~15% above consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: The Coreweave bond yield and CDS spike raised worries about financing costs weighing on capex commitments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler results (META Oct 21, MSFT/GOOG/AMZN Oct 28-29) that fail to show accelerating AI demand and OCF to push CDS spreads lower.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy is up over 50% YTD and was top of UBS's REVS framework heading into September.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher oil raises demand-destruction risk and lowers the upside value of owning Energy stocks. Energy has rallied more than forward oil.

theme_stances.key_argument: Equities have greater asymmetry to lower rates than higher, since the valuation reset has largely happened and AI and capex earnings growth offset higher discount rates.
theme_stances.evidence: equities are more resilient to higher bond yields now than in the past

theme_stances.key_argument: AI-related and broadening capex, with OCF up ~$825bn y/y, supports Industrials and Cap Goods even at higher rates.
theme_stances.evidence: We believe AI related industrial demand will remain robust amid higher rates

theme_stances.key_argument: Energy is up over 50% YTD and has rallied more than forward oil, with demand destruction risk at higher oil prices.
theme_stances.evidence: Time to start reducing Energy exposures.
